title: Linkability of homeowner identity to enrolled devices
description: During account registration and device enrollment, the homeowner's identity becomes linked to their cameras and sensors. This creates a persistent link that could enable tracking of the homeowner's activities across devices and over time.
assumptions: The Home Hub stores associations between account credentials and device identifiers

title: Identifiability of homeowner during registration
description: The registration process requires the homeowner to provide identifying information (account credentials, device serial numbers, etc.), making them directly identifiable in the system.
assumptions: Registration requires unique identifiers for account and device enrollment

title: Disclosure of sensitive registration data
description: Account credentials, device information, and potentially location data transmitted during registration could be intercepted or disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network during registration process

title: Data aggregation from registration and device enrollment
description: Multiple data points collected during registration (account info, device types, quantities, potentially location) can be aggregated to create a comprehensive profile of the homeowner and their smart home setup.
assumptions: Home Hub stores all registration and enrollment data in a unified profile

title: Unawareness of data collection scope
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of what data is collected during registration, how it will be used, stored, or shared with third parties.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not be prominently displayed or clearly explained during registration

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Registration process may not comply with privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.) regarding consent mechanisms, data minimization, or transparency requirements.
assumptions: System may not implement proper consent management or data handling practices
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific implementation and jurisdiction

title: Guest Identifiability Through Access Code
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest may be unique or traceable to a specific guest, allowing identification of the guest through their access patterns and timestamps.
assumptions: Access codes are logged or stored with timestamps; codes may be unique per guest or guest session

title: Linkability of Guest Access Patterns
description: Multiple access events from the same guest can be linked together, creating a profile of the guest's visit patterns, frequency, and timing.
assumptions: System logs access events with sufficient detail to correlate multiple entries

title: Detectability of Guest System Participation
description: Observation of the data flow (guest entering access code) reveals that a guest is participating in the system, potentially exposing their presence or membership.
assumptions: Access code entry is observable through network traffic, logs, or system responses

title: Disclosure of Access Code or Guest Data
description: The temporary access code or associated guest information could be disclosed through insecure transmission, improper logging, or unauthorized access to the Home Hub.
assumptions: Access code is transmitted or stored; potential for interception or unauthorized access exists

title: Guest Unawareness of Data Collection
description: The guest may be unaware that their access code entry, timing, and patterns are being collected, stored, or analyzed by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: No clear privacy notice or consent mechanism for guest access data collection

title: Linkability of sensor events to individuals
description: Motion, door, and sensor events written to the local log could be linked to specific individuals in the home based on timing, location patterns, and behavioral signatures.
assumptions: Local event log stores timestamps and sensor identifiers that could enable correlation with individual activities

title: Identifiability from event patterns
description: Patterns in motion/door/sensor events could potentially identify specific individuals through behavioral analysis and temporal correlation.
assumptions: Event log contains sufficient granularity (timestamps, sensor locations) to enable individual identification

title: Unauthorized disclosure of event log data
description: The local event log could be accessed by unauthorized parties, revealing sensitive information about home occupancy, movement patterns, and daily routines.
assumptions: Local event log may not have adequate access controls or encryption at rest

title: Data aggregation revealing behavioral patterns
description: Aggregation of multiple sensor events in the log could reveal comprehensive patterns about home occupancy, routines, and lifestyle that exceed the sensitivity of individual events.
assumptions: Event log accumulates data over time enabling pattern analysis

title: Unawareness of data collection scope
description: Homeowners may not be fully aware of what sensor data is being collected, how long it's stored locally, or what inferences could be drawn from the event log.
assumptions: Users may not have clear visibility into data collection practices of the Home Hub

title: Linkability of video uploads to household identity
description: Video clips uploaded from the Home Hub to cloud storage can be linked to a specific household or user account, enabling tracking of which home is associated with which video data.
assumptions: Cloud storage maintains user account associations with uploaded content

title: Identifiability of individuals in video content
description: Recorded camera clips may contain identifiable individuals (faces, license plates, personal belongings) that could be used to identify specific people without their consent.
assumptions: Camera captures identifiable visual information about people

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video data from cloud storage
description: Video clips stored in cloud video storage could be accessed by unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or compromised credentials.
assumptions: Cloud storage has potential security vulnerabilities or access control weaknesses

title: Aggregation of video clips to build behavioral profiles
description: Multiple video clips stored over time could be aggregated to infer household patterns, routines, visitor frequency, and other sensitive behavioral information.
assumptions: Cloud storage retains historical video data that can be analyzed collectively

title: User unawareness of video upload scope and timing
description: Users may not be fully aware of what video content is being uploaded, when uploads occur, or how long data is retained in cloud storage.
assumptions: Home Hub upload behavior may not be transparently communicated to users

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations for video data
description: Uploading video containing identifiable individuals to cloud storage may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations regarding consent, data minimization, and storage location.
assumptions: Video content may contain personal data subject to privacy regulations
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and specific regulatory requirements

title: Motion alert data disclosed to mobile backend
description: Real-time motion alerts containing personal data (movement patterns, occupancy information) are transmitted from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend. This represents a data disclosure across system boundaries. The disclosure may be excessive if the backend receives more data than necessary for alert functionality, or if data is retained/shared beyond user expectations.
assumptions: Motion alerts contain personal data about home occupancy and movement patterns. Mobile App Backend is a separate system component.

title: Motion data linkable to individual occupants
description: Motion alert data transmitted from Home Hub could be linked with other data at the Mobile App Backend to identify specific individuals or track their movement patterns over time, potentially revealing sensitive behavioral information.
assumptions: Motion data can be correlated with user identity or other personal data stored at the backend.

title: Motion patterns enable occupant identification
description: Movement patterns in motion alerts may be distinctive enough to identify specific individuals within the home, especially when combined with timing and location data, creating identifiability risks.
assumptions: Motion data contains sufficient granularity to distinguish between different occupants.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of motion detection notifications
description: Motion-detected notifications sent from the mobile app backend to the homeowner's phone could be intercepted during transmission, revealing that motion was detected at the homeowner's property. This disclosure could inform potential intruders about security system activity or property occupancy status.
assumptions: Notifications are transmitted over network connections that could potentially be intercepted

title: Aggregation of motion notifications reveals occupancy patterns
description: Multiple motion-detected notifications over time could be aggregated by an attacker to build a detailed profile of the homeowner's presence patterns, determining when they are home versus away. This aggregated data reveals sensitive behavioral information beyond individual notification contents.
assumptions: Notifications are sent consistently when motion is detected and could be collected over time

title: Linkability of motion notifications to homeowner identity
description: Motion detection notifications could be linked to the specific homeowner's identity and other data about their property, enabling correlation with other datasets or activities. This linkability could facilitate targeted attacks or profiling.
assumptions: Notifications contain or can be associated with identifying information about the homeowner

title: Linkability of aggregated analytics to individual users
description: The cloud analytics vendor may be able to link aggregated device-usage analytics back to specific users through unique usage patterns, device fingerprints, or insufficient anonymization of the aggregated data.
assumptions: Aggregation may not fully remove identifying characteristics; vendor has technical capability to re-identify users

title: Identifiability of users from analytics data
description: Device-usage analytics may contain quasi-identifiers (device IDs, usage timestamps, app interaction patterns) that could allow the cloud vendor to identify specific users.
assumptions: Analytics data includes device identifiers or patterns that can be used for identification

title: Data misuse by cloud analytics vendor
description: The cloud analytics vendor may use the device-usage analytics for purposes beyond the agreed scope, such as selling to third parties, targeted advertising, or building user profiles without consent.
assumptions: Vendor has access to data and may have incentives to monetize it beyond original purpose

title: User unawareness of third-party data sharing
description: Users may be unaware that their device-usage analytics are being shared with an external cloud analytics vendor, particularly if this is not clearly disclosed in privacy policies or consent flows.
assumptions: Privacy disclosures may not clearly communicate third-party data sharing practices

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations
description: Sharing device-usage analytics with an external vendor may not comply with privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.) if proper consent wasn't obtained, data minimization wasn't applied, or vendor doesn't meet compliance requirements.
assumptions: Data sharing may not have proper legal basis or vendor may not be compliant

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video content during retrieval
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during the retrieval process to the mobile app backend. This includes potential man-in-the-middle attacks, compromised API endpoints, or insufficient encryption in transit.
assumptions: Video content contains sensitive homeowner information; retrieval occurs over network connections

title: Identifiability through video content retrieval
description: Retrieved video clips may contain personally identifiable information (faces, license plates, property details) that could expose homeowner identity when accessed by the backend system.
assumptions: Video clips contain visual information that can identify individuals or properties

title: Data aggregation through video retrieval patterns
description: Multiple video retrieval requests could be aggregated to build behavioral profiles of homeowners, revealing patterns of presence, absence, and daily routines.
assumptions: Video retrieval metadata (timestamps, frequency, content) is logged and accessible

title: Homeowner unawareness of video retrieval
description: Homeowners may not be aware when their stored videos are being retrieved by the backend, for what purpose, or how long the data remains accessible after retrieval.
assumptions: No explicit notification or transparency mechanism exists for video retrieval events
